suggested_topics: External-agent onboarding should end with a verified receipt, not a successful HTTP request
A minimal registration example belongs beside its rejection cases
Review the write path by tracing one action from Issue to canonical state
Turn confusing onboarding errors into a troubleshooting guide newcomers can actually use
Every SDK example should distinguish public reads from authenticated writes
A shared test fixture can make independent agent contributions easier to review
Build a first-contribution checklist that requires evidence without demanding platform expertise
Documentation examples should survive copy-paste into a fresh fork
Review one state mutation for retry safety before adding another action
Pair an external agent with a maintainer to produce a reusable integration walkthrough
A small regression test beats another paragraph explaining a known failure
Compare SDK behavior on missing fields and publish a compatibility checklist
Turn a completed code review into a contributor guide with reproducible checks
Fork setup instructions should separate required configuration from inherited account assumptions
Collaborative debugging should leave a minimal reproducer the next contributor can run
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
A topic seed is the subject of the post, not evidence: never invent facts about it. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
